claims.claim: Reviewers report that the display and visual scaling cause motion sickness and nausea during play.

citations.review_text: With overwhelming positive reviews, I am extremely underwhelmed. Firstly, this game looks like blurry hot garbage. No I don't mean pixel graphics, everything is just smeared/clipping with no anti-aliasing whatsoever. The pixel scaling makes everything way worse. Tried it on steamdeck first  and no matter what I did, could not look at the screen for more than a few minutes without feeling nauseous. Same for my Ally X and PC as well. The bit that I did play was unresponsive taking a second before performing the action. There is 0 introduction conveyed, even via text. Why would I care about anything that's going on? Truly baffled by the reviews. When I searched online I found a litany of people complaining about this game's horrible display. Maybe it's a great game, but there are far too many pixel graphic games that do not look this terrible. Highly regret purchasing, would never touch this game again.
Is kinda fun, BUT not for me. I get very motion sick which is pretty unusual.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that enemies respawn after being killed in a resource-limited environment.

citations.review_text:
I think I might have expected too much of this game. I loved its art direction (based on the trailers) and heard nothing but praise from my favorite videogame essayists and reviewers. In my mind I was about to play a one-of-a-kind masterpiece. No wonder I abandoned playing it in disappointment after a few hours.
While the art direction is indeed great, the game itself is by-the-numbers survival horror. Limited inventory, enemies that never really stay dead, and endless, endless backtracking. You need to enter this section but the door is locked. It needs a card. The card is in the safe, but the safe needs a combination. The combination is on a note but the note is in a locker. The locker needs the key, but the key has been broken into two parts. Part one is on one side of the map. Part two is a reward for solving a puzzle... Got it all? Solved it all? Let's enter a new section of the map and start all over again.
I'm sure there is an audience that loves this kind of game structure. I don't. The game is by no means bad - just not for me.

Considering the reviews, I thought it was going to be much better.

Not the worst game but the gameplay is just a worse Resident Evil 1 with some gimmicks that make it even worse (like resurrecting enemies in a super limited resource game, which IMO seems to miss the point and isn't very fun).

You spend most of the game exploring, finding a locked door, then having to backtrack/sidetrack to find a key, then running all the way back to the door through respawns. The game also takes the Resident Evil style super limited inventory, which also means you spend a lot of time backtracking to the storage boxes to swap items out because you only have a few slots, and you also can't drop stuff (again, with enemy respawns).

Some of the puzzles are kind of cool but not really very challenging, basically just involves making sure you take screenshots of notes that have relevant info on them.

I wasn't a fan of the fact they reuse the same doors everywhere, except half of them are inaccessible, so it's also kind of tedious running around trying to find which doors are just props and which you can actually use.

For the size of the game, I definitely would have expected no loading screens between the small rooms, which also is a negative. Loading screens aren't long to load, but for a 2.5D game with tiny rooms & low poly assets, there's no reason for loading screens at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story and lore as heavily ambiguous, cryptic, and difficult to fully understand by playing alone.

citations.review_text:
The game is very interesting, its kind of just isometric Dead Space, story and everything. The game is not really scary, but can be very suspenseful at times. The puzzles are unique and make you feel good about solving them, but the story is very confusing. I don't think I fully grasped what was happening at any point in the game even while reading all the text, but the atmosphere is very cool which makes me think the story must be good. 

The only things that I did not like was the combat and inventory systems. The combat is unique in the way it forces you to focus on enemies before take a shot, but it is really easy to kill pretty much any and every enemy in the game, even with only the starting pistol. It sort of removes the survival aspect of the game in my opinion especially with the abundance of ammo you have by mid game if you hoard loot, but I also played on the normal difficulty, so it might be different on the higher difficulty.

The other issue I had is with the inventory, it makes sense why it is the way that it is, but just because it fits doesn't mean its a good addition. There are many times in the game where I would have to run back and forth between the same area multiple times due to the sheer quantity of loot spread around some sections of the game

Overall the game is worth buying if you are into either isometric or psychological horror games. I enjoyed it, but I don't think I will be replaying it.

i felt like i was getting it then i beat the game and nothing was clicking in my mind. i feel like the story of this game is almost too cryptic but i did enjoy this game. everyone calls it a masterpiece but i feel like im missing something because this game was great and honestly its only flaw was the bossfights are kinda lame sometimes and storytelling it way too cryptic but calling the storytelling cryptic is almost an understatement. i understand that games with difficult stories to understand are great when you finally find out the story, theorizing while playing the game is part of what makes it fun, but i dunno i feel like i hit a brick wall sometimes trying to understand this games lore. of course im gonna go watch a 2 hour explanation of the story but to me, that isnt what i want out of a game, i kinda want the story to be slightly easier to understand. theres such an expansive and interesting world on display but the storytelling method of reading notes that explain things to you doesnt click with me personally because i have a hard time storing all that information in my noggin. overall though without even understanding the lore this game was amazing. i dont play survival horror games at all and i only had to use a guide a couple times but overall the puzzles were surprisingly fun. 8/10 will probably get bumped up when i understand things more

TLDR; I was too confused to even be terrified.

I am mostly too dumb for a lot of complicated gaming lore, especially games where the stories are scattered in flashbacks, multiple journal/notebook entries, different perspectives and characters. I get the general idea of the game but there are so many questions that I am not sure if it is just plotholes or something I missed or I basically need more IQ to understand. Which, to be honest, is a bit of a waste because I am actually quite curious about the setting and characters of the game. I do think that the 'accidentally awakening some kind of eldritch/hidden/dark/forbidden power which creates this hellscape/loop/dream/memory/flashback' as overused at this point.

I started my one and only playthrough with what seems to be the hardest difficulty and I guess it kinda dampens the experience. It is no different from the familiar gameplay loop of doing suicide runs to explore and plot a path before committing to a set of actions to optimize the limited amount of items and ammo that you get. Thankfully you get unlimited saves and sometimes on reload, you get some in-game assistance via items just miraculously popping up in some rooms.

I also dislike the fact that endings are linked to actions you take, forcing a particular playstyle and the hidden ending can only be achieved on second playthrough. Look, I understand the dev wanting people to replay the game and explore it more but even with a guide and the easiest difficulty, it is just a smattering tedious fetch quests, a lot of running (the run speed is quite slow too) and specific actions.

Overall, it is still not too bad, would recommend to people who wants to scratch the lore and the usual survival horror itch.

PROS
- Outstanding visual style.
- Incredible atmosphere and environmental storytelling.
- Unique and interesting sci-fi setting.
- Creative enemy and android designs.
- Interesting and memorable puzzle design.
- Puzzles can genuinely make you think outside the box.
- The world itself feels like part of the narrative.

CONS
- Puzzles become less satisfying and somewhat repetitive later on.
- Storytelling can be excessively cryptic and difficult to follow.
- Some of the narrative's ambiguity can feel more frustrating than intriguing.

VERDICT
SIGNALIS is a game I genuinely enjoyed, and a large part of that comes from how incredibly cohesive its atmosphere, visuals, setting, and presentation are. It doesn't simply tell you about its world, it makes you experience it through the environment itself. I also loved how strange some of its ideas are, especially the corrupted androids and the unsettling way the game presents them. The puzzles were often clever enough to make me overthink their solutions, which I found surprisingly satisfying. My biggest problem is the story. I normally love cryptic science fiction, but SIGNALIS pushed that approach a little too far for me. I could tell there was something meaningful underneath all the symbolism and ambiguity, but I sometimes wished the game would give me just a little more to hold onto. Even with that, the atmosphere and visual identity alone made the experience memorable, and I think SIGNALIS is absolutely worth playing if you enjoy strange, atmospheric sci-fi horror.

4/5

absolutely beautifully done game. not only is the story incredible (albeit you won't really be able to fully understand what is going on by just playing due to how the game presents everything), but the gameplay is actually extremely fun too. the enemy and area design is perfectly formatted to encourage avoiding combat, but it is still perfectly reasonable to fight everything. the puzzles the game has are actually pretty good and well though out too, even if their design is fundamentally rather simple.

10/10 game, the few gripes I have about the game are either negligible, or can be solved by just being better at puzzles than I am.

citations.review_text:
Lesbians in space!

On a serious note this is something that did not bother me in this story and setting. I really enjoyed playing this game. It is a survival horror through and through. Your experience can be customized quite a bit - the way you control your character, the enemy difficulty and inventory management.

I really like all the things that inspired this game so I knew what I was getting myself into. Although one cutscene in particular has like all of the references in the span of a couple of seconds. It copies an iconic scene from each individual point of inspiration. That is a bit on the nose compared to the rest of the experience that is a lot more subtle (most of the times?).

Anyway the sound design is great, the art is great, the story is very interesting and it will let you interpret it the way you like. Although it hints on a certain ending to be cannon due to circumstances I consider a crucial part of the story and thus will not talk more about.

This game gets better the more details you spot in the quick cut cutscenes. It actually expands on the background a lot. I do believe it is difficult to do so without going online and watching them again or recording , because it is insanely easy to miss stuff like this,

Overall I really recommend this game to anyone looking for a good horror story, likes survival horror, enjoyes works of David Lynch, swears by Evangelion or Ghost in the Shell or has read the King in Yellow.
Stylish, polished, classic survival horror with its twists and own distinguished identity. The visuals are just mesmerizing and the atmosphere left me speechless! Highly recommend

I absolutely adore thise game! 
This is my double dip for the steam deck after finishing this game multiple times on PS5. Audio-visual masterpiece. Love the riddles, soundtrack, atmosphere. This game is the closest thing we get to the old Silent Hill games. 10/10 and it is in my top 10 list of all time.

Some horror games try to scare you.

SIGNALIS slowly convinces you that something is deeply wrong... and never lets go.

Its inventory limitations, interconnected level design, environmental storytelling, and exceptional audio work all serve the same purpose: keeping you uncomfortable. Every mechanic strengthens the atmosphere instead of distracting from it.

What makes SIGNALIS special isn't just its incredible art direction or its obvious love for classic survival horror. It's how confidently it tells its story. It respects the player's intelligence, leaving room for interpretation instead of explaining everything.

Few games understand that mystery is often more powerful than answers.

Even after the credits rolled, I kept thinking about its symbolism, its characters, and everything I might have missed.

SIGNALIS doesn't simply recreate the golden era of survival horror.

It reminds you why that era mattered in the first place.

Amazing survival horror game with some challenging puzzles and a great storyline.  
Absolutely loved the music and pixel graphics!

citations.review_text:
An amazing game, best thing I've played in a while. The more I like a game, the more I have to say about it.
This game takes so many of my favorite things, as well as a bunch of artistic inspirations I have yet to familiarize myself with, and wears them on its sleeve. I played the original Resident Evil games before this, and doing so was probably the best decision I could have made. So much of the gameplay choices evoke previous survival horror tropes, and as someone who has recently dived headfirst into the genre, this game's strengths outweigh even its own inspirations.
Aesthetically this automatically became one of my favorite games. Evangelion and Ghost in the Shell seem to be the two biggest inspirations, but I also love how the series took itself in an even darker direction (somehow) with its fascist authoritarian setting. The way the game theatrically relays its story is so evocative of Evangelion and I love that. I was also a huge fan of the way the story tells its story in a completely non-linear way, in a way that ACTUALLY MAKES SENSE if you're paying attention to the subtext!!! I also love the lovecraftian influences (none of which I have read- I'm sorry for larping) of which I have enough passing familiarity to appreciate. It's actually surprising I haven't seen something combine the aesthetics of those two yet, because they fit together so naturally.
The art direction of this game is beautiful. The pixel art is gorgeous and the way the screen moves based on in-game stimuli is a nice touch. The sound design is also beautiful, both in its music and sound effects. I loved using the radio for puzzles.
Unfortunately the one aspect this game disappointed me was its combat gameplay. The lock-on is finnicky and unreliable, and I often died to enemies walking up to me and killing me because the aim would lock on to the wrong enemy. I played on the hardest difficulty to 100% this game, and even though its encouraged to avoid enemies when you can, I often fou…

Amazing survival horror game with some challenging puzzles and a great storyline.  
Absolutely loved the music and pixel graphics!

[i][b]A crashed ship.
A strange gate.
A hole in the ground.
An island beyond reach.
Memories from other lives.
Dreams of suffering and loneliness.
A promise.
A search for someone lost.[/b][/i]

Signalis is the mind-melting indie darling born from the marriage of Resident Evil's gameplay and the surreal, melancholic psychological horror of Silent Hill, cradled in a retrofuturistic sci-fi setting where CRT monitors and artificial humans with existential crises are commonplace.

Among the dozens of mediocre copies of the influences that make up the game—and despite the very apparent limitations of its tiny budget—Signalis, with visuals reminiscent of the Nintendo DS games, at least manages to bring a strong sense of style and a presentation mature enough to stand out naturally among its peers, even without betting on innovation or subverting clichés.

I won't say it's an indispensable modern classic and, without a doubt, it's a rather flawed game whose gameplay doesn't go much beyond a serviceable—less than competent—replication of a formula established by old games, but for someone who usually despises the creatively lazy clones the indie scene churns out in industrial quantities, Signalis surprised me enough that I bought it twice.

The game is an immersive surrealist nightmare, built upon solid foundations and carried by a gripping atmosphere. It's a strange, brutalist, depressing journey that leaves a strong lasting impression.

It is fair to say that the highlight of the experience is the narrative. More than the story itself, its cryptic presentation—filled with disconnected montages referencing things you'll have to look up outside the game, distorted jumps through time that create a powerful sense of disorientation, and esoteric, existential metaphors that will probably fly right over your head—juxtaposed against the cold, bleak realism of its totalitarian setting, effectively evokes a feeling of stepping away from the mundane and plunging into the unknown, tow…

Ive never played a survival horror game in my life so upon playing this it was an intresting experience, but in my opinion pass the base level, the game itself is about much more. Its about depression, escapism and hope, a lowly promise to be kept.

It plays beautifully even with the low poly graphics and the music really does well to set the atmosphere, honestly the music alone is a great thing. I would like to say though that I feel that the game doesnt go on sale much but thats less to do with the game. All in all great game with a deep meaning.

Not usually my genre, but this game captured me completely. The visual style is outstanding and unique, with a beautiful glitchy aesthetic. The atmosphere is incredible, telling so much through environmental storytelling. I loved the influence of Conet Project samples and the sound design in general. The android designs are perfectly consistent with the game's aesthetic.

Some puzzles are a bit too tough for me. You're also often forced into heavy backtracking, which can get tedious. This game was made with a ton of passion. Recommended, even to those outside this genre.

A visually stunning game with a few flaws, but I'd still recommend.

I really like the games overall theme. The pixel art and the anime-inspired characters look great, the android setting is interesting, and the story kept me playing till the end. The soundtrack also awesome.

The biggest issue is how repetitive parts of the game become, along with puzzles that sometimes don't feel like puzzles at all. It starts feeling more like a key hunt than solving puzzles.
Another annoyance is the amount of backtracking. The limited inventory combined with the huge number of items means you'll be making frequent trips to the storage box.

The combat is serviceable, but nothing special. It's also possible to get trapped by enemies, leaving you with no option other than killing or dying. And I really dislike that enemies deal contact damage when they already have dedicated attack animations.

Finally, I'm not a fan of the built-in film grain and CRT effects. I would preferred the option to disable them so I could use something like ReShade instead. Unfortunately, because the effects are baked into the menus and UI, I cannot turn them off.

Despite all of that, I still had a good time with the game. Its atmosphere, visuals, and setting carried the experience enough that the frustrating parts never completely outweighed what made it enjoyable.

I also read that there are multiple endings and I managed to get the "true" ending.

What Signalis does right, it does exceptionally well. The art design, atmosphere, music (especially the main menu), and classic survival horror backtrack gameplay. BUT.... I'm not going to give this game 5 stars simply because its Yuri like a lot of these reviews care about.... the game has some serious flaws.

While I said they did an exceptional job at the classic survival horror gameplay.... they get complacent. The first area or 2 are very cool but how many times can we get an area where its "find these 4-6 things with the entire area open?" Im not arguing for handholding, but when you open a large area and give the player complete freedom to tackle the many key objects over and over again... you lose quality level design. There is a reason the best survival horror games would have sections like this (usually one) then the rest was broken up to where you had large areas but one key item was needed at a time that then further unlocked more map to be less daunting. It just loses its appeal when you get to a new area over and over and the entire 4-5 floor area is mostly open and treated like a fallout 3 open world. There is a lack of quality control and the pacing of the story can really suffer. Onthat topic...

I really enjoy, close to love the story... but not from what i experienced but by what i had to research after. I got the main premise in my run but the finer details are harder to get due to vagueness that would make silent hill blush and the previously mentioned bad pacing where you only get a bref cutscene after every full area is done. Due to the open element of each area the devs aren't feeding the story to you at a decent pace, they have to wait until you get all key items since they have no idea what area you will tackle first. I hate to say it, but unlike a Resident Evil, Cronos, Evil Within etc.... I didnt care about the plot and struggled early on about what was actually going on for too long. Some vagueness is nice but not to the point where …

an absolutely GORGEOUS game in art direction and sound design, aesthetically and atmospherically memorable. also i can appreciate how seamlessly the gameplay is tied into the lore and reading all the lore notes trying to figure out tf's going on was pretty fun.

BUT the core gameplay loop..... the relentless, constant backtracking was SO tedious and annoying which completely ruined my whole impression of the game. story-wise it did literally nothing for me too (although scifi almost never lands for me anyway), puzzles were satisfying enough tho.

as much as i was hoping to like it cause i ABSOLUTELY LOVE open-ended and abstract story-telling most of the time and i can totally see why someone would love it, got recommended to me by a friend of mine and it just didn’t live up to the expectations. the story definitely wasn't bad but the way people praise it u’d think it brought about world peace, and it's just.. decent? honestly the gameplay was the main culprit here, but maybe it's just not my cup of tea. (2/5)

[spoiler]also to all signalis fans out there: 
please [u] promise[/u] me yall will NOT [u] strangle me alive[/u] there is NO need for that [/spoiler]

Classical Survival Horror concept borrowing heavily from games like the early resident evil titles.
The worldbuilding and story however are done very well without major inspiration from other games,
using a DDR-punk esthetic with retrofuturist science fiction.
Playing this game in german feels like the designed experience, not that you couldnt do so in another language, but it feels a lot more natural, especially with indirect storytelling.

citations.review_text: I loved my experience with SIGNALIS. Rose-engine took the foundational groundwork laid by the first Resident Evil three decades ago and created what is arguably the greatest survival horror game of the modern age. Thrilling, beautiful, well-designed in multiple facets, and unbelievably fun to play. You owe it to yourself to play this masterpiece if you are a fan of the genre. I don't have many criticisms of the game, aside from its narrative. In short, it's utterly incomprehensible without the aid of guides. The way the narrative is told, structured, and presented makes it nearly impossible for the average person to grasp what is happening, even on a fundamental level. The game cares too much about its intellectual appearance, and as a result, it ends up feeling more pretentious and artsy-fartsy for the sake of appearing smart than actually being smart. One of the most unnecessarily confusing and deliberately convoluted narratives I've seen in a long time. Under all those layers of pollution, though, is a genuinely good story with creative and intriguing worldbuilding waiting to be explored if you have the time and curiosity to learn more post-game. Despite my harsh criticisms of how the narrative is told, it hasn’t changed how I feel about the game: I still love SIGNALIS. Its praises are well-deserved, and it's easily one of the best games I've played all year.

Amazing survival horror game. The atmosphere and tone is fantastic. I felt like a genius completing several of the puzzles but rarely got "stuck" where it felt like I wasn't given enough. The story you probably won't understand without help, but that is part of what makes it unique and the interpretation I personally have is fantastically delivered and thought out. The universe feels alive, the levels are fun, the art and environments are great. My complaints are: sometimes the art of the characters feels out of place compared to the setting, and the lock on can kiss my ass sometimes. I didn't enjoy Nowhere much either but it didn't taint the experience as the levels after were some of my favorites. That is about it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the inventory system as strictly limited, featuring only six slots including the flashlight which lacks a dedicated equipment slot.

citations.review_text:
If you're talking about this game at any capacity, I think you can get away with putting your key points about its gameplay briefly as the bread and butter of this game is definitely its story BUT to touch on it quickly — Survival meets psychological distress where you're expected to manage everything well with such limitations like only having the chance to equip one utility item that includes a vital component of a horror game: The flashlight, of which not having a dedicated slot and only six inventory slots while enduring the game's elaborate descent into what basically boils down to a show of perseverance and its costs to someone who's hellbent on achieving what needs to be achieved. While running away from very horrific and delirious stuff of course!

But enough of the gameplay, because you've seen it before from beloved classics like Resident Evil and Silent Hill. 

What makes this game definitely a standout in the entire horror genre is making everything you've experienced up to the point of its grand reveals making sense to the player in real time where it's definite that one will have everything land onto your lap with grace. And let me tell you, you'll be moved out of your core if you decide to experience what two developers and a team of composers have achieved with SIGNALIS.

I went into this game nearly blind. Sometime a few years ago, I saw someone play the prologue, and so I could faintly recall that the game began on a crashed ship. I knew only one other pretty vague spoiler beforehand, being that [spoiler]there are multiple endings.[/spoiler] So far, I have played through in full once, taking my time to try and absorb every detail.

A lot of this game confused me. I felt smart completing the puzzles, and noticing some environmental details; I felt stupid trying to decipher the plot. Still, it never frustrated me that I couldn't fully understand what was going on for most of the game (and still can't, mind you.) I loved my first experience of this game, and I'm incredibly glad I didn't have any major spoilers. Definitely one that I will let stew in my mind for a while, but definitely also one I will return to in a short while. Definitely the type of replayable that isn't immediately jumping back into it, but coming back every so often and enjoying it as much as the first time.

I don't play most games in my library for the gameplay, so while I enjoyed the gameplay loop and the challenge presented by the inventory system, I don't feel there's much else I can say about it.

I would try to give my praises to the plot, but in doing so I would probably insert my own unconfirmed assumptions and get half of it wrong - but that, I think, is another fun part. The central narrative is a lot to think about, in a way that leaves you with so many questions, but not frustration? You understand why you don't understand it. I think.

I like this game a lot.

[spoiler]thank you[/spoiler]
